summary: Points out a possible deadlock in the Initial Connection Protocol. If both sides issue one request and wait for a match before the second, the first requests may not match, and a deadlock can occur when both open send or both open receive sockets.

plainLanguage.summary: Two hosts can become stuck if each sends one connection request and waits for the other to match it. This note recommends changing when each side sends its requests so setup can continue.

subtitle: A warning about a possible deadlock during Initial Connection Protocol setup.

tldr.problem: The Initial Connection Protocol can deadlock if both sides issue one request and wait for a match before issuing another.
tldr.mechanism: The note recommends that the server make its socket requests before waiting and that the user issue its requests without waiting for the server between them.
tldr.outcome: It also prioritizes requests involving sockets S and U+3 if a host must pause between requests.

sections.title: How the Deadlock Can Happen
sections.content:
The RFC describes a possible deadlock in the Initial Connection Protocol (ICP). If both sides issue one request for connection and wait for a match before sending a second request, their first requests may not match.

A deadlock occurs in particular if both sides open their send sockets first or both open their receive sockets first.
sections.plainLanguage: Each host can be waiting for a request that the other host has not sent. If both follow the same mismatched order, neither can continue.

sections.title: Recommended Request Order
sections.content:
The RFC recommends that the server perform steps 7 and 8 before waiting for the user to perform step 6 or 7. It also suggests that the user issue the requests in steps 6 and 7 without waiting for the server.

If the user is only listening, both listens should be issued without waiting for the server. If a host must pause between requests, it should issue the requests involving sockets S and U+3 first.
sections.plainLanguage: The server should send its later requests before it waits. The user should also send its requests without waiting after each one.

sections.title: Scope of the Note
sections.content: This short note identifies an ordering hazard in the ICP described in the cited Current Network Protocols document and recommends how hosts should order requests. It does not replace the complete ICP description.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC focuses on one setup hazard and how to avoid it. It refers readers to the separate ICP specification for the complete procedure.
